messages.subject: Combining/joining genlights
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,
I'm looking to join multiple genlights with the same loci but different individuals.
I looked into gl.join(), but it seems to want both loci and inds the same?

I have simulated two datasets from my sample data using gl.sim.ind(), those two sim datasets were then used to simulate offspring using gl.sim.offspring(), and now I need to combine the 3 sim datasets into a single genlight. Is there a function for this/anyone have a readymade solution?

Thanks in advance,
Deane.

Thanks Dale and Renee for your suggestions.

I’m embarrassed to say that when I retraced my steps I had no problem running the gl.subsample.loci function, and it worked whether I pre-removed monomorphic loci or included the mono.rm command in gl.subsample.loci.

I suspect that there was some minor format problem in my input genlight yesterday that has now been remedied.. The only thing I can think I may have done wrong yesterday is to run the gl.compliance.check function without saving it – i.e. x.gl <http://x.gl> <- glcompliance.check(x.gl <http://x.gl>) not just glcompliance.check(x.gl <http://x.gl>), which I think just reports.

In any case…the function is not broken Arthur!

Thanks again…

Cheers,

Olly

messages.body_plain:
Hi Olly,

I would have got to it. Yes, gl.compliance.check takes a genlight object and, by assignment, makes a new compliant genlight object. It is a bummer, but it fixes two problems. 1. the constraints placed on us by CRAN in getting the new dartR compliant with their requirements led to loss of backward compatibility in placed and 2. we did a major overhaul anyway that trashed backward compatibility were it not for the gl.compliance.check script.

All the best, and have a good break.

A

messages.subject: duplicate loci tolerance
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Not a bug, but I have discovered that the format-changing-output functions differ in whether they tolerate duplicate loci (i.e. gl2..other-data-format functions)

Specifically gl2genalex gives an error message if you have loci with duplicate names, but for example, gl2structure doesn’t. The error message is slightly cryptic, but it does point to the number of loci as a problem, and the error disappears if you remove the duplicate loci.

Of course there shouldn’t be duplicated loci ;-), but some seemed to have slipped through the cracks in one of my datasets, and until I removed them the gl2genalex function didn’t work.

It wasn’t too hard to remove the duplicates semi-manually, but I recall that there used to be a function that did it. Would you consider reinstating it?

Cheers and Merry Xmas!

Olly
